claims.text: Parseable, schema-valid output does not guarantee a correct task result, so the benchmark scores structure and task quality separately.
Across the five tasks, overall schema validity was lower than most readers would assume and task quality was lower still.
Three of the six implementation conditions kept near-ceiling schema validity and the highest quality; the other three scored well below them.
The differences are findings about whole system configurations, not about library features in isolation.
A team choosing between these libraries should compare them on its own task contracts.

numbers.comparison: PydanticAI, LangGraph and DSPy versus the plain SDK, Agno and CrewAI

limits_authors.text: Results do not generalize beyond synthetic business tasks to long-lived agents, production databases, regulated decisions or adversarial inputs.
The human audit packet has not been reviewed.
The benchmark is not a security or deployment certification.

likely_overclaims: That PydanticAI, LangGraph or DSPy cause higher quality; the authors say the contrasts are not causal attributions to library features.
change_for_agents: Treat schema validation as an admission gate and add a separate task-level check; do not read a passing schema as a correct result.

compact.claim: Schema validity and task quality are separable: parseable output does not establish correctness, and six Python implementations differ widely under one shared contract.
compact.method: Five business-workflow tasks run through six Python implementation conditions with one model, a frozen analysis plan and a 5,400-row primary matrix.

results.finding: 0.684: overall schema validity; 0.638: mean automated quality
0.91–0.94: mean quality for PydanticAI, LangGraph and DSPy

compact.limits: Synthetic tasks, one primary model family, human audit packet unreviewed.
